title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1% vs regular)
drivers.evidence: Same price level (4.56) in 2026-09-28: sales were 195 vs baseline 207.6 → x0.94. No prior 5.1% increase at this price level, but consistent with downward trend. Noise-adjusted effect shrunk to -6.0%.

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: No historical evidence of social media driving lift. Not seen before. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk to x1.0.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 207.6. No events in target week. Price is 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular 4.34), which is above prior promotion levels. Past promotions (10–30% off) had noise-adjusted lift x1.36; this price increase is likely to suppress demand. TikTok trend is unverified and not backed by past data—no historical lift from social media. No promotion or holiday driver. Classical model suggests x1.0, but price increase likely reduces sales. Use noise-adjusted price effect: prior 5.1% increase (2026-09-28) led to x0.94 vs baseline. Apply modest downside. No evidence of new trend. Confidence is medium.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.7 - 290.1 | 10%-90%: 156.4 - 280.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
